title: Algorithm Design Flowchart
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Computational Thinking
Algorithm Design
Flowcharts
Scratch
description: Clickable top-to-bottom flowchart of the five moves of algorithm design: understand the goal, decompose, find patterns, order the steps and check that it finishes. Clicking a box explains the move and shows what it looked like for the square-drawing example. A loop from the decision diamond back to move 2 shows what to do when an algorithm does not finish.

learningObjectives: Given a new drawing problem, name the five moves of algorithm design in order and say what you would do at each move.
prerequisites: An algorithm is a list of steps, in order, that always finishes

controls.label: Flowchart boxes
controls.description: Click a box to show what that move means and what it looked like for the square

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Clickable worked example used as a checklist for a new problem
keyQuestions: What are the five moves, in order?
What would you do at each move to design a triangle-drawing algorithm?
Where does the 'no' arrow go, and why does it not go back to move 1?
commonMisconceptions: If an algorithm does not work you have to start over from nothing. You only go back and break the problem down again.
The order of the steps is a small detail. Order is the algorithm.
assessmentOpportunities: Ask the student to name the five moves in order with the chart covered.
Give a new drawing problem and have the student write one sentence per move.
